item.stem:
Nila looks at the diagram of $\triangle ABC$. Two interior angles are marked $58^{\circ}$ at $B$ and $47^{\circ}$ at $C$.

Which claim correctly finds the remaining interior angle at $A$?

options.A: Angle $A$ is $58^{\circ}$, because that is the parallel-line label for this triangle.
options.B: Angle $A$ is $180^{\circ}-(58^{\circ}+47^{\circ})=75^{\circ}$, using the other two interior angles of the same triangle.
options.C: Angle $A$ is $58^{\circ}+47^{\circ}=105^{\circ}$, treating the sum of the known angles as the missing one.
options.D: Use an exterior-angle supplement at a neighbouring polygon instead of the two interior angles of $\triangle ABC$.
